$comment: Bibliography for muscle records. `key` is cited from data/muscles-*.json. `notes` points at the reading notes in papers/ (tracked); `pdf` names the local PDF (git-ignored).

sources.authors: Abdala V, Diogo R
sources.title: Comparative anatomy, homologies and evolution of the pectoral and forelimb musculature of tetrapods with special attention to extant limbed amphibians and reptiles
sources.role: Primary source for the pectoral/forelimb homology matrix (their Tables 1–3) across Caudata, Anura, Testudines, Lepidosauria, Crocodylia, Aves.

sources.authors: Diogo R, Molnar J
sources.title: Comparative anatomy, evolution, and homologies of tetrapod hindlimb muscles, comparison with forelimb muscles, and deconstruction of the forelimb–hindlimb serial homology hypothesis
sources.role: Primary source for the pelvic/hindlimb homology matrix (their Tables 1–8) and for the critique of forelimb–hindlimb serial homology.

sources.authors: Molnar JL, Diogo R, Hutchinson JR, Pierce SE
sources.title: Reconstructing pectoral appendicular muscle anatomy in fossil fish and tetrapods over the fins-to-limbs transition
sources.role: Fin-to-limb polarity: which pectoral muscles were present in sarcopterygian fish, which appeared at tetrapodomorph and crown-tetrapod nodes.

sources.authors: Diogo R, Johnston P, Molnar JL, Esteve-Altava B
sources.title: Characteristic tetrapod musculoskeletal limb phenotype emerged more than 400 MYA in basal lobe-finned fishes
sources.role: Primary source for the ancestral fin muscle set and for the Latimeria, Neoceratodus and Polypterus columns. Supplies the one-to-one homology hypotheses linking fish fin muscles to tetrapod limb muscles.

sources.authors: Mansuit R, Herrel A
sources.title: The evolution of appendicular muscles during the fin-to-limb transition: possible insights through studies of soft tissues, a perspective
sources.role: Muscle architecture (mass, PCSA) across the fin-to-limb transition, binned into the four abductor/adductor × superficialis/profundus groups. A Perspective piece; its own data are a literature meta-analysis, not new dissection.

sources.authors: Molnar JL, Diogo R
sources.title: Evolution, homology, and development of tetrapod limb muscles
sources.role: Review of methods and confidence levels for reconstructing muscles in fossils; source of the confidence vocabulary used here.

sources.authors: Diogo R, Ziermann JM
sources.title: Muscles of chondrichthyan paired appendages: comparison with osteichthyans, deconstruction of the fore–hindlimb serial homology dogma, and new insights on the evolution of the vertebrate neck
sources.role: Chondrichthyan outgroup condition for paired-appendage muscles.

sources.authors: Ziermann JM, Miyashita T, Diogo R
sources.title: Cephalic muscles of cyclostomes (hagfishes and lampreys) and Chondrichthyes (sharks, rays and holocephalans): comparative anatomy and early evolution of the vertebrate head muscles
sources.journal: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society 172: 771–802
sources.role: Deep outgroup polarity for cranial muscle homologies (mandibular, hyoid, branchial arch series).

sources.authors: Ziermann JM, Diogo R
sources.title: Development of head muscles in fishes and notes on phylogeny–ontogeny links
sources.journal: In: Johanson Z et al. (eds), Evolution and Development of Fishes. Cambridge University Press, ch. 10
sources.role: Developmental origin (arch identity) and innervation of gnathostome head muscles.

sources.authors: Werneburg I
sources.title: The cranial musculature of turtles
sources.role: Source of the turtle cranial muscle records (his Appendix 1: 94 muscular units with origin, insertion, function, innervation and an exhaustive synonym list).

sources.authors: Sefton EM, Bhullar B-AS, Mohaddes Z, Hanken J
sources.title: Evolution of the head–trunk interface in tetrapod vertebrates
sources.role: Developmental origin of the cucullaris / trapezius complex and the head–trunk muscle boundary.

sources.authors: Naumann B, Warth P, Olsson L, Konstantinidis P
sources.title: The development of the cucullaris muscle and the branchial musculature in the Longnose Gar
sources.role: Actinopterygian developmental data on cucullaris and branchial muscle origin.

sources.authors: Gambaryan PP, Kuznetsov AN, Panyutina AA, Gerasimov SV
sources.title: Shoulder girdle and forelimb myology of extant Monotremata
sources.role: Monotreme attachment data — the intermediate condition between the reptilian and therian pectoral girdle.

sources.authors: Ercoli MD, Álvarez A, Stefanini MI, Busker F, Morales MM
sources.title: Muscular anatomy of the forelimbs of the lesser grison (Galictis cuja), and a functional and phylogenetic overview of Mustelidae and other Caniformia
sources.role: Therian forelimb attachment and action data, with muscle mass fractions.

sources.authors: Molnar JL, Diaz RE Jr, Skorka T, Dagliyan G, Diogo R
sources.title: Comparative musculoskeletal anatomy of chameleon limbs, with implications for the evolution of arboreal locomotion in lizards and for teratology
sources.role: Squamate limb muscle attachments in a derived arboreal grasping form.

sources.authors: Navarro EA, Quipildor M, Quinteros S
sources.title: Description of the neuroanatomy of the brachial plexus in South American lizards. Phylogenetic implications
sources.role: Squamate brachial plexus composition — the innervation backbone for lepidosaur forelimb records.

sources.authors: Bishop PJ, Pierce SE
sources.title: Late acquisition of erect hindlimb posture and function in the forerunners of therian mammals
sources.role: Stem-synapsid hindlimb muscle reconstruction and posture inference.

sources.authors: Allen V, Molnar J, Parker W, Pollard A, Nolan G, Hutchinson JR
sources.title: Comparative architectural properties of limb muscles in Crocodylidae and Alligatoridae and their relevance to divergent use of asymmetrical gaits
sources.role: Crocodylian limb muscle architecture and attachment data.

sources.authors: Kępa et al.
sources.title: Thoracic limb myology of the Komodo dragon (Varanus komodoensis)
sources.role: Varanid forelimb attachment and action data.

sources.authors: Fahn-Lai P, Biewener AA, Pierce SE
sources.title: Broad similarities in shoulder muscle architecture and organization across two amniotes: implications for reconstructing non-mammalian synapsids
sources.role: Direct monotreme–lepidosaur shoulder comparison used for synapsid bracketing.

sources.authors: Sigurdsen T, Green DM, Bishop PJ
sources.title: Did Triadobatrachus jump? Morphology and evolution of the anuran forelimb in relation to locomotion in early salientians
sources.role: Anuran forelimb and pectoral girdle function, including landing-force muscles.

sources.authors: Fritzsch B
sources.title: Evolution and development of extra-ocular nerves and muscles in vertebrates
sources.role: Extraocular muscle and nerve evolution. NOT peer reviewed — used only as a pointer to primary literature.

sources.authors: Freitas Pereira R, Pereira dos Santos J, Lima FC
sources.title: Pectoral and forelimb myology of Iguanidae
sources.role: Iguanid forelimb attachment data.
